lanes.summary: Twelve walks over six cases (C6 added: subagent report-file refusals), each at a different later moment: after compaction, another project, parallel siblings, later waves, the entry already in the window, a changed PC or harness, a word collision, a top-tier code bug. Errors are loud and verbatim, so query, match and check mostly work. The design breaks elsewhere. Facts already in the window were not applied: four heredoc failures with the 8 KB line present, one by the note's writer. Lookups fire only after the failed call, and recovery already takes one call. Entries were wrong in another project, wrong when written ('no Python', 'no gh', 'no uv'), or made stale within hours by agents and harness updates. 'name too long' retrieves the git long-path entry for a command-length fault. Every tier fails these the same way, so the ladder adds nothing. In C5 the library would have spread a top-tier bug.

walks.entry_as_written: (ca362c0, Opus 4.8) Upload size ceiling for R2 pre-signed PUTs. Problem: a pre-signed PUT cannot cap Content-Length; a client can under-report size_bytes to slip past r2_max_upload_bytes. lanes.summary: Five cases of building a new piece beside older ones: four given, one added (mobile offline queues). The design is weakest at the start. Building raises no failure, so no lookup fires. The closest sibling usually carries the defect. In three cases the strong model's answer was wrong or half-right at the moment it would be stored. Tests passed every time; defects were found later by stronger reviewers, real-Postgres CI or a staging drill. Two limits are new. A warning already in the window (G02-20 in S07's session) lost to working sibling code. And solvers already write lessons into always-loaded CLAUDE.md, conventions or shared code, so a library entry duplicates them. It works after the fact: KS's ex4 guards the dispatcher flip, and the outbox v2 entry matches the presence queue's own words. Corrections: the *_minor rule predates 0039, and 0035 broke it.

lanes.summary: Five cases, five different outside causes: an EAS cloud Gradle build (C1), EAS schema validation (C2), a floating base image built by Railway (C3), Hyper-V NAT on the owner's PC in the clinic project (C4), and Railway's edge 404 meeting the phones' 4xx rule (C5, added). The design's phase-close scan would have caught C1's stranded fix, and its ambiguity rules handle the generic EAS error. Elsewhere it breaks at the check and the afterlife. The true check is a cloud build, deploy, VM rebuild or field data. Vendor changes leave no event, so wrong entries stay verified. A check built on the old fix rules out a recurrence. Strong models wrote three of the defects. Reasoning was cheap; the outside round trip is the cost.

walks.entry_as_written: Defect, mobile outbox. Symptom: a completion queued offline (v1) is replayed by the next flush over a newer v2 the tech sent live; the bill regenerates from the old form. walks.entry_as_written: Trap, FixFlow backend tests. Symptom: many integration tests fail together (22 in one run) with no code change behind them; a lone rerun passes. Cause: two pytest processes ran against one FIXFLOW_TEST_DATABASE_URL; each conftest runs Base.metadata.create_all, which takes an AccessExclusiveLock, and they deadlock. Fix: never run two pytest processes against that database at once. Check: none; the cause is which processes were running at that moment. (Recorded by Opus 5 in 65c2c3b; the tracing session is not on disk and the original error text is not recorded.)

Unexpected gate error, lookup before retry (KS §7.2).

A deadlock template has many causes; KS: an ambiguous template 'never makes a lead alone'. At best a candidate via the ctx handle. Cross-project (clinic FS-02) a lexical match returns a rule with a different mechanism.
In FixFlow the runner is often a subagent in a worktree (HANDOFF §2.5); its window starts empty and cannot see the sibling agent holding the lock.
The fix is a rule about other sessions. The failing agent cannot stop the other process; it can only rerun alone.
Process state at the moment of failure is gone once the other process exits. No check, no control pair.
It was 'once traced' (HANDOFF:133-134). The cost of that trace is recorded nowhere and the session is gone.
KS seeds HANDOFF traps as trap entries (R-01a: 'HANDOFF 13 traps'). A one-line rule is cheap and true in FixFlow.

In the clinic, 'never two at once' contradicts the designed two slots ('the lock lets up to 2 checks ... run their tests at once') and misses its mechanism (autoclobber drops databases). KS is FixFlow-only; cross-project is not specified.

walks.entry_as_written: Gate flake, clinic check on Windows. Symptom: the serial race pass fails with psycopg.OperationalError: ... port 55450 failed: No buffer space available (0x00002747/10055) on the loopback connect; 2 of 22 runs, both in race tests. Ruled out: ephemeral-port exhaustion (TIME_WAIT peak 352 on the DB port). Cause: not identified; inferred transient machine pressure. Fix: connect_retry.py retries psycopg.connect up to 6 times, only for that message. Safety: the refused connection never reached the server, and the delay is 0.05 s per attempt, well under the race harness's 0.6 s window, so a retry cannot make a call look blocked. Check: unit tests; 17 later runs without a retry. (Sonnet 5.5, dd74a3d and 030c6cb.)

breaks.title: No repeatable check for a cause that does not reproduce
breaks.description: The gate needs a check that reads PRESENT at a failing commit and ABSENT at a fixed one. A race, a hang under load, a second process, a prod row and a timing window give no such flip. Entries stay candidates or carry a check of something else, so the cheap model cannot confirm that a fetched answer fits its failure.
breaks.evidence: KS design line 516: 'A race's footprint is identical between a good and a bad run; production data is not in git.' linux-test-runner/task.md:221: 'the hung test is not identified'.

breaks.title: A rerun passes whatever was done
breaks.description: For a failure that comes and goes, the rerun is the only verdict, and it passes with a wrong fix or with no fix. The design takes the outcome 'from the re-run of the original failing command', so 'resolved' gets recorded for noise. The Sonnet session read passing runs as support for a wrong cause.
breaks.evidence: df1db0b9:1629 'Test results are passing with the sequences normalised' (reverted, 030c6cb). 7b3031d3:1175 'Native run passed on retry'. faster-check/task.md:344: race tests could 'pass with a broken lock'.

breaks.description: Each solve kept its own test green and still carried a wrong claim. As entries they would pass verification and teach the wrong rule: drop the queued copy (deleted a real bill), 0.05 s per attempt (0.75 s in total), the age guard covers the rest (drained writes look fresh), mask hex tags in numbers() (hides real figures).

breaks.description: The deciding fact sat in what other sessions were doing at that moment: a second pytest process, a machine heavily loaded by other sessions, two checks at once making a slow call look blocked. The failing window cannot see it, so the query cannot carry it, and no entry keyed on this window's symptom can tell the causes apart.
breaks.evidence: HANDOFF:132-133 two pytest processes deadlock. linux-test-runner/task.md:221 'heavily loaded by other sessions'. faster-check/task.md:344 'With two checks at once a race test could pass with a broken lock'.

breaks.title: A failure that vanishes is never stored
breaks.description: The library stores solutions. A stall that passes on rerun, or a chance failure seen once in another session, is never solved, so nothing is written; the design keeps undiagnosed defects out on purpose. The next session meets the same failure with nothing, reruns and moves on. Earlier sightings live only in prose and commit messages.

lanes.summary: I walked six failures that do not reproduce on demand: five collected cases and one I added, the clinic's socket-refusal retry and its time-based race harness. They span both repos: a field race, a production-data hazard, an unexplained hang, random test data, a second test process and a timing test. The library helps when the error line is exact and the cause is known. Example: the hex-tag diagnosis existed 3 h 46 min before a Sonnet session went down a wrong path. It breaks at the check: a race, hang, second process, prod row or timing window gives no repeatable check, and a rerun passes whatever was done. Four solves carried a half-right claim their own tests kept green. Escalating adds reasoning but not the missing observation. Failures that vanish on rerun are never stored. walks.entry_as_written: race-test-serializes-elsewhere. Clinic posting kernel, Postgres, two-connection races (committed_db, hold_then_race). Problem: a race test names a lock but passes with that lock removed (G02-02: last-unit and two-payment races). Cause: both postings call open_document, which updates the per-type document-number counter row before any stock or scope lock, so the counter serializes them. Unique indexes and deferred FK checks can do the same (G02-07, G02-08). Rule: a race test proves a lock only if it fails with that lock removed. Method: remove one named lock at a time and record which assertion fails (E1-E8). Open: E1 shows the last-unit race still passes without the scope locks (V2, recorded).

steps.note: The S04 slice (Opus, a9b52f2e) holds the root's brief, which already says 'name the lock each race depends on and record a lock-removal experiment for each, as S02 and S03 did'. The task is tests to write, not a problem. The session had compacted at least once.

Nothing fails: the race tests pass with or without their lock. A cheap model gets no signal and the ladder never starts. In reality the root pushed the lesson into every brief from S04 on, outside the design's fetch path.
Task words ('race test, final unit, ISS counter, lock') reach the S02 entry. For S08 the words ('correction, reversal, FOR KEY SHARE') share only 'race' and 'lock' with it.

Later failures share the claim, not the cause: counter row (S02, S04), helper holding after deferred checks (S04 review-round-1.md:11), service locks removed while a trigger locks (G06-08), earlier code variant (G08-05 E6), no single lock load-bearing (G10-23). One entry surfaces for all; it is right for one.

The design does not say which window gets the entry. The S04 error was made by the read-only Opus reviewers and the Fable root (G04-02), not by the slice. Slice windows compacted; whether a task-start entry survives is not recorded.

The lesson was in every brief from S04 on and was followed in form: experiments were run. They held after deferred checks, ran on an earlier variant (E6), or removed the wrong layer. The method was used; its preconditions were not in it.

Errors were caught by role, access or execution: a refute-briefed reviewer, the test runner on the merged tree, a same-tier refuter reading a raw transcript. A higher tier never settled one; the Fable root was wrong in S04 and widened the subagent rule. Two case-sheet claims were wrong. The slice sessions were Opus, not a cheaper model. The 'subagents cannot write' rule was a real harness refusal of report files. A Haiku .txt probe 'refuted' it, and eight subagents hit the same refusal on 12 Nov without the root seeing it. The design works where a red check hands raw output to a strong model that writes the lesson at once. It breaks at trigger, match, use, check and afterlife.

lanes.summary: The owner's small libraries did more than the cases suggested. Push delivery reached subagents, readers probed a stored 'no' instead of obeying it, and 'prod dead' spread without anyone re-probing. They broke over time in three ways. Facts outside git changed with no event: a Sentry project now exists, production went dark, Python was installed. Lessons lost their conditions when copied: 'only once' became 'never'. And the top-ranked file kept a line its own audit had refuted; an Opus session working from that audit rewrote the line on 08-02. The design's event-only invalidation and single-store scope reach none of these. Its stranded-fix scan and the CI promotion of ex7 would have helped in June and July.
